articles.title: Carbon Tow Spread
articles.summary: Spread-tow carbon ribbons in rectangular lanes; flat glossy lanes with faint tow edges, low relief, subtle sheen. Reads as a soft diagonal-striped satin sheen; the ribbons merge into a directional carbon-tape glow.
articles.what: Spread-tow carbon ribbons with rectangular fiber lanes. Up close: Long straight diagonal ribbons, running up-right at about 35 degrees, 8-20 px wide with sharp hairline edges, like flat spread carbon tapes laid side by side. On metal they stripe the highlight with bright and dark lanes; on satin they are a faint ghost of lines. From a distance: Reads as a soft diagonal-striped satin sheen; the ribbons merge into a directional carbon-tape glow. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Carbon Tow Spread".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, spoiler and splitter
Long panels where the diagonal can run uninterrupted
Numbers stay readable; lanes are narrow and soft.
Faint: subtle diagonal lines across the highlight
Pairs well with: gloss, matte, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not woven carbon: lanes are long unbroken diagonal ribbons, no over-under
Not brushed metal: lanes have defined edges and varied widths
Avoid: very subtle at distance, lane direction must match panel.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.goal: Layer Carbon Tow Spread over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Kevlar Blue Hybrid
articles.summary: Satin aramid-carbon weave, yellow and blue-black tow crossings, matte sheen Reads as a smooth sheen with a faint silky fabric grain; the weave is gone beyond arm's length.
articles.what: Aramid-carbon hybrid weave with satin yellow and blue-black tow crossings. Up close: Extremely fine woven cross-grain, a diagonal crosshatch of micro lines just a few pixels apart, visible inside the highlight band as a faint fabric texture. Too fine to see individual tows; the blue and yellow of the name do not exist in a shine map. From a distance: Reads as a smooth sheen with a faint silky fabric grain; the weave is gone beyond arm's length. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.

pitfalls: Not a colour weave: it adds no blue or yellow, only shine texture
Not visible carbon twill: tows are too fine to read
Avoid: subtle, needs good lighting, yellow may clash with livery.

articles.title: Nomex Honeycomb Core
articles.summary: Open honeycomb cells with resin-wet edges, faint hexagonal grid catching soft highlights. Reads as a soft geometric grid in the highlight only; the lines vanish quickly and the car looks plain with a faint faceted sheen.
articles.what: Open honeycomb composite core with resin-wet cell edges. Up close: A fine triangular or hex lattice of thin light lines, cells about 40-60 px across, drawn like a wireframe grid. Faint on satin; on metallic the lines show as bright seams across the highlight and dark seams in the floor reflection. From a distance: Reads as a soft geometric grid in the highlight only; the lines vanish quickly and the car looks plain with a faint faceted sheen. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.

articles.title: Prepreg Resin Bleed
articles.summary: Regular parallel wavy bands in clearcoat; low contrast, faint rippled sheen, tiny coverage. Reads as a smooth sheen with a faint cross-hatched shimmer in the highlight; the lines vanish with distance.
articles.what: Prepreg pinholes, resin bleed lines, and glossy trapped clear. Up close: Faint criss-crossing hairline lines forming a loose diagonal net, like fine fabric or craquelure, visible in the highlight. In the floor reflection a few wandering dark wavy lines run across, like wavy resin runs. From a distance: Reads as a smooth sheen with a faint cross-hatched shimmer in the highlight; the lines vanish with distance. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
